name: AST-Precise Localization
question: Exactly which lines need to change?
summary: Instead of reading whole files or grepping text, the agent parses code into an abstract syntax tree and navigates by structure: the function, its callers, the class it belongs to. It loads and edits only the nodes involved, which saves context, avoids broken edits and speeds up finding the fault.
useCases: Coding agents working in large repositories
Bug fixes that start from a stack trace or failing test
Refactors that must touch every caller of a function

items.detail: signatures of classes and functions, not full bodies
file → class or function → lines (as in Agentless)
replace a node, then re-parse to validate

steps: Build a repo map of symbols and signatures with tree-sitter
Localize top-down: candidate files, then functions, then line ranges
Load only the selected nodes plus their immediate context
Validate every edit by re-parsing and running the tests
pitfalls: Dynamic code (reflection, metaprogramming) hides real call paths
Parsers lag behind new language syntax
Too narrow a view misses side effects in other files
remember: Navigate by structure, edit by node.
caption: Token counts are illustrative. The saving grows with file size.

code.text: repo_map = [s for p in python_files("app/") for s in symbols(p)]
issue = "Tax is wrong on invoices above INR 1 lakh"
files = llm_rank(issue, sorted({p for p, _, _ in repo_map}))[:3]
funcs = llm_rank(issue, [s for s in repo_map if s[0] in files])[:1]
callers = find_references(path, name)       # LSP or ast-grep

steps.title: Build a repo map
steps.text: Parse every file with tree-sitter and keep only class and function names with their line numbers: 340 files become about 4,100 symbols.

steps.title: Localize the file
steps.text: Given the issue text, the model ranks files from the map, not from full source. billing.py comes first.

steps.title: Narrow to the function
steps.text: Inside billing.py it picks Invoice.apply_tax. The syntax tree gives its exact span: lines 42 to 57.

steps.title: Add the immediate context
steps.text: Find-references returns two callers, one in export.py. Function plus callers is 56 lines, about 560 tokens, against 30,000 for the whole file.

steps.title: Edit the node, then re-parse
steps.text: The patch replaces only that function’s bytes. Re-parsing confirms the file still has no syntax errors before anything is saved.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: The billing tests pass. The change touched 15 lines, and a reviewer can read the whole diff in a minute.

pros: Loads a few hundred tokens instead of whole files
Finds definitions and callers precisely, unlike text search
Edits replace exact nodes, so unrelated code is untouched
Re-parsing catches broken edits before tests run
cons: Dynamic code (reflection, metaprogramming) hides call paths
Grammars lag behind new language syntax
Too narrow a view misses side effects elsewhere
More tooling to build and maintain than plain file reads
avoidWhen: Small repositories where whole files fit comfortably in context
Languages or templates with no reliable parser

playgroundGuide.scenario: A bug report says tax is wrong on invoices above INR 1 lakh. The fault is in Invoice.apply_tax, a 16-line function in billing.py. It has two callers: Invoice.total() in the same file and to_csv() in export.py, 20 lines each. The fix changes rounding, so both callers must be checked. Code costs about 10 tokens per line, and the model’s first edit happens to leave a bracket unclosed.
controls: Choose how the agent loads code: the whole file, a text search, or a syntax-tree lookup.
With the syntax-tree lookup, choose whether to add callers, and whether to re-parse edits before tests.

presets.name: Whole file
presets.expect: 3,000 lines load 30,000 tokens, 23% of the window, and only 1% is relevant. export.py is never read, so the fix is incomplete.

presets.name: Text search
presets.expect: 38 matches with 10 lines either side: 798 lines, 7,980 tokens, 7% relevant. Both callers are found, but among a lot of noise.

presets.name: Syntax tree + callers
presets.expect: 56 lines, 560 tokens, 100% relevant. Both callers are covered and re-parsing catches the broken edit at once.

presets.name: Too narrow
presets.expect: Only the 16-line function: 160 tokens and 100% relevant, but to_csv() is missed, so exported invoices stay wrong.

tools.best: Fast, error-tolerant parsing of source code into syntax trees, for most popular languages.
tools.ex: Build a repo map of every class and function with its line range in a few seconds.
pros: Bindings for Python, Rust, JavaScript and more
cons: Syntax only: no types or cross-file resolution

tools.best: Structural search and rewrite using patterns that look like code.
tools.ex: Find every call to apply_tax($X) across the repository and rewrite it to apply_tax($X, rounding="half_up").
cons: Pattern matching, not full semantic analysis

tools.best: Go-to-definition, find-references and symbol search with real type information.
tools.ex: Ask pyright for every reference to Invoice.apply_tax, including one reached through an alias.
cons: Servers are heavier to run headless

tools.best: A ranked, token-budgeted map of the repository’s files and signatures sent with each request.
tools.ex: Aider sends a 1,000-token map so the model can ask for exactly the files it needs.
pros: Budgets the map to fit context
cons: Ranking can miss rarely referenced files

tools.best: Studying hierarchical localization: rank files, then classes and functions, then edit locations.
tools.ex: Reproduce its file → function → line localization on a handful of your own issues.

library.name: tree-sitter
library.what: Fast, error-tolerant parsers for 100+ languages. Used by editors and by coding agents to build repo maps.

numericDrill.question: A file has 3,000 lines at about 10 tokens each. The target function is 16 lines, and its two callers are 20 lines each. How many tokens does AST localization load?
numericDrill.answer: (16 + 20 + 20) lines × 10 = 560 tokens, against 30,000 for the whole file: about 50× less context.

interview.question: Why isn't grep enough for code localization?
interview.answer: Grep finds strings, not structure: it can't tell a definition from a call or a comment, misses renamed imports, and returns noisy matches. Syntax trees and language servers resolve symbols, scopes and references precisely.

interview.question: What is a repo map?
interview.answer: A compact summary of a repository: files with their classes, functions and signatures (not bodies), often ranked by relevance, so the model can decide where to look without reading whole files.

mistakes.mistake: Sending whole files to the model
mistakes.fix: Send the relevant nodes plus immediate context
Re-parse after every edit and run the tests

quiz.question: A stack trace points to line 812 of a 5,000-line ledger.py, inside post_entry(). What should the agent load first?
options: The post_entry function node and its callers
The last 100 lines of the file
quiz.explanation: The tree gives the enclosing function exactly; callers show how its behaviour is used.

quiz.question: A file has 4,000 lines at about 12 tokens each. The faulty function is 30 lines, with 3 callers of 15 lines each. How many tokens does AST localization load?
quiz.explanation: (30 + 3 × 15) lines × 12 tokens = 75 × 12 = 900 tokens, against 48,000 for the whole file.

quiz.question: What can a syntax tree tell the agent that grep cannot? Select all that apply.
options: Whether a match is a definition, a call or a comment
The exact start and end of a function
Which class a method belongs to
The runtime value of a variable
quiz.explanation: Trees capture structure. Runtime values need execution or debugging.

quiz.question: The claims code dispatches events with getattr(handler, "on_" + event). What is the risk for AST-based localization?
options: Static references miss this call path, so add text search, traces or tests
quiz.explanation: Dynamic dispatch builds names at runtime, so no static reference exists. Cover it with other signals.

quiz.question: What is a repo map?
options: A compact list of files with their classes and function signatures, not full bodies
quiz.explanation: It lets the model decide where to look without reading whole files.

quiz.question: A vulnerable deserialize() function must be found at every call site across 2,000 files. Which approach fits best?
options: Read every file into the model
Structural search with ast-grep or find-references from a language server
quiz.explanation: Structural search and references find calls precisely, including ones plain text search would confuse with comments.

quiz.question: After a model edit, re-parsing the file reports ERROR nodes. What should happen next?
options: Save the file and let the tests find it
Reject the edit and ask the model to retry before writing anything
Ignore it: parsers are often wrong
quiz.explanation: A syntax error is cheap to catch at parse time; there is no point running tests on a broken file.

quiz.question: In what order does Agentless-style hierarchical localization narrow down the fault?
options: Files, then classes or functions, then edit locations
quiz.explanation: Top-down narrowing keeps each step’s context small.

quiz.question: Which are good practices for structural edits by an agent? Select all that apply.
options: Replace the node’s byte range rather than rewriting the file
Run the tests that cover the changed code
Let the model rewrite the whole file from memory
quiz.explanation: Rewriting whole files invites unrelated changes. Node-level edits plus validation keep changes small and safe.

quiz.question: You fix rounding inside compute_brokerage(). Why load its callers as well?
options: They may rely on the old behaviour and need changing too
quiz.explanation: Too narrow a view misses side effects: a caller that rounds again would now double-round.

quiz.question: An agent reads a 2,500-line file (10 tokens per line) 8 times per task. Localization cuts each read to 600 tokens. At $3 per million input tokens, how much does it save per task?
quiz.explanation: Whole file: 25,000 × 8 = 200,000 tokens = $0.60. Localized: 4,800 tokens ≈ $0.014. Saving ≈ $0.59.

quiz.question: Why is tree-sitter popular for coding agents?
options: It is fast, supports many languages and still produces a tree for code with syntax errors
It resolves types across the whole program
quiz.explanation: Error tolerance matters because agents often work on half-edited files.

quiz.question: A legacy module is written in a language with no maintained parser. What is the sensible approach?
options: Fall back to text search and larger context, and lean harder on tests
Invent a grammar in the prompt
quiz.explanation: AST precision needs a parser. Without one, use coarser tools and stronger verification.

quiz.question: Which can find the call sites of a function across a whole repository? Select all that apply.
options: Parsing only the current file with tree-sitter
quiz.explanation: References and repository-wide structural search cover all files; parsing one file only sees that file.

quiz.question: A monorepo holds about 40 million tokens of code and the context window is 200,000. What should the agent see first?
options: A budgeted repo map of relevant files and signatures
quiz.explanation: A small ranked map lets the model choose where to look.

quiz.question: Two classes each define apply_discount(). How does a syntax-tree approach avoid editing the wrong one?
options: It uses the qualified name, such as Policy.apply_discount
It picks the first match in the file
It asks the user every time
quiz.explanation: Trees know which class each method belongs to, so names can be qualified.

quiz.question: When does too narrow a view cause a broken fix? Select all that apply.
options: A changed return type breaks callers in other modules
A config file read at runtime still has the old key
Renaming a local variable used only inside the function
A database migration is needed alongside the code change
quiz.explanation: Side effects outside the node are the risk. A purely local rename is safe.

quiz.question: A repo map lists 1,200 files, 6 symbols per file on average, at about 12 tokens per signature. How big is the full map?
quiz.explanation: 1,200 × 6 × 12 = 86,400 tokens, which is why maps are ranked and budgeted.

quiz.question: What was a key idea behind SWE-agent?
options: An agent–computer interface with a windowed file viewer, search commands and edits rejected if they break syntax
Training a new model from scratch
quiz.explanation: Designing the interface the agent uses, including a lint check on edits, improved results substantially.

quiz.question: Which signals are good starting points for localizing a bug? Select all that apply.
options: Keywords and identifiers in the issue text
The number of stars on the repository
quiz.explanation: Traces, failing tests and issue text all point at code. Popularity says nothing about the fault.
